sourceReview.summary: No concrete P1/P2 found in the reviewed port helper, integration callsite or cleanup paths. The prepared process.c differs from the supplied pinned base by exactly the proposed patch payload. The raw per-executable REG_SZ append and caller ownership contract are preserved while the reviewed unterminated-data, odd-size and allocation-arithmetic defects are addressed.
sourceReview.comparisonMethod: Read-only unified diff of the complete prepared and supplied base files; exact comparison with the port patch payload after its descriptive preamble. No patch application, build or project-code execution.

reviewEvidence.subject: Original per-executable raw append contract
reviewEvidence.observation: The helper keeps slash/backslash basename lookup, HKCU Software\Wine\AppDefaults\<basename>, CommandLineAppend, KEY_QUERY_VALUE and REG_SZ-only selection. It creates cmdline + one space + the suffix through its first NUL. It introduces no environment expansion, argument tokenization or re-quoting. Missing/wrong-type/empty/oversized values and allocation failure leave the existing command line in use, as with the original helper.

reviewEvidence.subject: Registry byte bounds and missing NUL
reviewEvidence.observation: The 1025-WCHAR array exposes only 1024 WCHARs of query capacity. Query status is saved before closing the opened key. Non-success, non-REG_SZ, shorter-than-one-WCHAR, over-capacity and odd-byte results return before reading value as a string. Accepted data is explicitly terminated at size/sizeof(WCHAR), which lies within the spare element even at full capacity. The later lstrlenW cannot scan uninitialized trailing storage. Existing embedded NUL behavior remains ordinary REG_SZ string behavior.
reviewEvidence.comparisonWithOldPatch: The old helper terminated only value[1023], leaving an uninitialized gap after shorter unterminated data and truncating a full unterminated last WCHAR. The new helper uses the actual returned byte count and reserves the extra terminator element.

reviewEvidence.subject: Registry handle lifetime and error buffer handling
reviewEvidence.observation: Every successful RegOpenKeyExW reaches RegCloseKey exactly once before subsequent helper returns. Failed opens do not close an unowned handle. C short-circuit evaluation of status prevents reading undefined type/data after query failure, including ERROR_MORE_DATA. There is one bounded query and no two-query size race.

reviewEvidence.subject: Size arithmetic and copy extents
reviewEvidence.observation: Lengths are converted separately to SIZE_T before addition. With value_len at most 1024, subtracting value_len+2 from floor(SIZE_MAX/sizeof(WCHAR)) cannot underflow on the intended 32/64-bit targets. The guard ensures len=command_len+value_len+2 and len*sizeof(WCHAR) fit before allocation. The prefix copy, one-space write and suffix-plus-NUL copy exactly occupy the allocation. The guard and allocation precede all output writes.
reviewEvidence.comparisonWithOldPatch: The old expression added lstrlenW int results before assignment to size_t and had no checked allocation-size bound.

reviewEvidence.subject: Key buffer sizing
reviewEvidence.observation: The unchanged basename restriction is length<MAX_PATH. The fixed Software\Wine\AppDefaults\ prefix is 26 WCHARs; at MAX_PATH=260 the largest accepted basename plus prefix and NUL requires 286 WCHARs, within key[MAX_PATH+40] capacity 300.

reviewEvidence.subject: Caller buffer and preexisting tidy buffer ownership
reviewEvidence.observation: The helper reads both input strings and returns a separate process-heap allocation only on successful append. The callsite frees the previous tidy buffer only when it differs from the caller cmd_line, and only after the replacement is allocated and fully copied. A null helper return retains the prior pointer and its ownership. The app_name-only synthesized command and get_file_name-owned quoted command follow the same existing ownership test.

reviewEvidence.subject: App name and command-line alias lifetime
reviewEvidence.observation: When application name is inferred, get_file_name writes it to the caller-local name array and returns either the original cmd_line or a separate quoted command allocation. Replacing/freeing an owned tidy command therefore does not invalidate inferred app_name. Explicit app_name remains borrowed from the caller, and caller cmd_line is not freed by the new branch.

reviewEvidence.subject: Normal and error cleanup
reviewEvidence.observation: All inspected returns before helper invocation are unchanged. After the helper, invalid current directory, process-parameter allocation failure, debug setup failure and invalid parent attribute go through done; process creation and fallback paths also converge there. done destroys parameters and frees tidy_cmdline only if it differs from the caller buffer. The ANSI wrapper subsequently frees its own converted inputs; the W path neither double-frees those inputs nor leaks its appended replacement.

reviewEvidence.subject: Scope of actual prepared changes
reviewEvidence.observation: The exact prepared/base diff has only the winreg.h include, the new helper and its post-name-resolution invocation. The existing done cleanup is unchanged. The source-level SIZE_T and registry declarations and kernelbase registry exports were also read from the supplied pinned tree; this is not compilation or link verification.

gsbaseReview.summary: The pinned x86_64 macOS source implements whole-GSBASE switching at the reviewed syscall, Unix-call, callback, signal and thread-start boundaries. Current canonical source preserves that dispatcher/start/callback mechanism. No concrete current legacy-slot ABI conflict requiring Highball0008/0009/0011 was found. Their mirror model must not be copied blindly: current TEB+0x340 already contains syscall_dispatch. This is a source mapping, not runtime acceptance or a change to v0 patches or user engines.

comparison.observationArtifactRole: The observation JSON was read for orientation. These conclusions come from the actual source, complete signal diff, ABI definitions, callback entry declaration and direct byte comparisons; no historical commit or old runtime claim was accepted solely from that JSON.

boundaryMapping.boundary: Thread initialization and first PE entry
boundaryMapping.mechanism: mac_thread_gsbase obtains the native pointer from THREAD_IDENTIFIER_INFO.thread_handle and releases its Mach port. init_syscall_frame saves it in amd64_thread_data.pthread_teb at TEB+0x320. signal_start_thread keeps the real TEB in r13, builds the syscall frame, calls initialization on the native side and jumps to the common dispatcher return, which installs the TEB GSBASE before PE startup.
boundaryMapping.canonicalRelation: This entire source tail is byte-identical, with canonical line numbers shifted by 42.

support.observation: TEB initialization sets Peb, Tib.Self=&teb->Tib and data->teb. The first NT_TIB member is at TEB offset zero.

boundaryMapping.mechanism: The entry reads the frame through gs:0x378 and the real TEB through gs:0x30 before changing bases. After saving the PE register state and moving to the kernel stack, the Apple branch loads pthread_teb from 0x320(r13) into rdi, zeroes esi and executes syscall 0x3000003. It reconstructs rcx from the saved frame base after the syscall clobber. Unix service and trace calls occur after the native base is selected; kernel-stack TEB accesses use the explicit r13 pointer.

boundaryMapping.boundary: Common syscall return, including context/instrumentation routes
boundaryMapping.mechanism: The Apple common return saves result rax in r8 and the frame pointer in rdx, passes the TEB in rdi to the direct TSD-base syscall, then restores rcx and rax. This precedes the ordinary ret, control/integer-context iret and instrumentation alternatives. The instrumentation entry joins the normal prolog; the exported return entry and startup path join this same common return.

The Unix-call entry obtains the frame and TEB while GS points at the TEB, saves its frame/register state, switches stacks and installs the saved pthread_teb before the Unix function call. The argument/table state used after the raw syscall is kept in registers not listed as syscall-clobbered by this source protocol.

boundaryMapping.boundary: Unix-call fast return and restore-flags return
boundaryMapping.mechanism: Nonzero low restore-flag bits branch to the common syscall return. The separate fast return also installs TEB GSBASE: it saves result rax in rdx and frame rcx in r14 across the syscall, restores both, restores the caller r14 from the frame, and restores r13/rdi/rsi before ret. This path was inspected independently rather than assumed covered by the common label.

call_user_mode_callback receives the real TEB as an explicit argument and holds it in r13. It sets up the nested frame, completes native trace work, switches to the user stack, preserves callback rcx in r10 across the Apple TSD-base syscall with rdi=TEB, then dispatches to the callback or instrumentation target. The actual PE KiUserCallbackDispatcher subsequently reads gs:0x60 for the PEB callback table.

boundaryMapping.boundary: PE callback return to outer Unix frame
boundaryMapping.mechanism: PE callback code calls NtCallbackReturn. ntdll.spec declares that entry as syscall 0x0005, so its ordinary syscall entry restores native GSBASE before the Unix NtCallbackReturn body calls get_thread_data and user_mode_callback_return. That helper restores the previous frame and returns into outer Unix code; it does not need a second local GS switch or the old host-slot restore.
boundaryMapping.limit: The source declaration and call chain were inspected, not a built/generated syscall stub.

boundaryMapping.mechanism: Handlers are registered SA_ONSTACK. Early thread data comes from rsp masked by signal_stack_mask, not pthread TLS. For a PE-associated thread init_handler sets native pthread_teb GSBASE before normal handler work. leave_handler installs TEB GSBASE only when the saved return stack is outside both the signal stack and the syscall/kernel interval; native/nested Unix returns retain the native base. Without a TEB, these routines do not synthesize a PE GSBASE.
boundaryMapping.relatedRecovery: check_invalid_gsbase at pinned lines 2182..2269 explicitly notes that macOS entry already replaced GSBASE, so it cannot report the original interrupted base; its recognized repair path relies on leave_handler to install the TEB. This is not proof of arbitrary GS modification recovery.

boundaryMapping.mechanism: defer_msync_signal uses the native signal-stack pointer and atomic data fields before init_handler and does not read/write GSBASE or call pthread TLS. A deferred return skips both init and leave, leaving the interrupted base unchanged. Nondeferred handlers still install native GSBASE at init_handler; private-fault containment is added there. The unchanged leave_handler retains the original return classification. These statements describe visible source operations, not compiled async-signal-safety or complete msync recovery verification.

TEBLayout.observation: NT_TIB64 places FiberData at 0x20 and Self at 0x30.
TEB begins with NT_TIB and places LastErrorValue at 0x68.

PEvsUnixAccessors.observation: x86_64 PE NtCurrentTeb reads gs:0x30; WINE_UNIX_LIB uses an out-of-line function. GetCurrentFiber uses the actual TIB FiberData field.
Native NtCurrentTeb returns get_thread_data()->teb, with get_thread_data using pthread_getspecific under the restored native base.

fiberUpdates.observation: ConvertFiberToThread, ConvertThreadToFiberEx and SwitchToFiber update the real TEB field and HasFiberData/state as appropriate. With PE GSBASE=TEB, direct gs:0x20 and these field accesses address the same storage, with no separate mirror needed.

lastErrorUpdates.observation: Internal GetLastError/SetLastError access DWORD at NtCurrentTeb plus 13 pointer slots, i.e. 0x68 for x86_64.
RtlGetLastWin32Error, RtlSetLastWin32Error and the combined status/error helper use the same real TEB field. Direct PE gs:0x68 accesses are therefore coherent under the whole-base source model.

initialFiberBoundary.observation: Pinned TEB initialization seeds FiberData with 0x1e00. This audit does not repeat the old patch prose assumption that an unconverted thread necessarily has NULL FiberData, or infer native Windows equivalence from that seed.

legacyPatchMapping.oldMechanism: PE fiber APIs mirrored TIB.FiberData into a host block at GS+0x20 while GS stayed native.
legacyPatchMapping.rV1SourceMapping: The whole base is the TEB during PE execution, so the current direct TEB fiber writes and intrinsic loads share one field. The old extra PE mirror stores are redundant in this model; no port of that helper is indicated by the reviewed source.

legacyPatchMapping.oldMechanism: Saved host_qos at TEB+0x340 and swapped the contents of GS+0x20 at individual crossings.
legacyPatchMapping.rV1SourceMapping: Whole-base transitions choose the intact native block or real TEB instead of copying slot contents. Syscall, independent Unix fast return, callback, signal and startup paths are present. The hardcoded old host_qos offset is not free: current amd64_thread_data.syscall_dispatch occupies 0x340 with an offset assertion.

legacyPatchMapping.oldMechanism: Added host_slot13 at 0x348, copied LastErrorValue to/from host GS+0x68 at crossings, and changed PE error accessors.
legacyPatchMapping.rV1SourceMapping: Whole-base PE accesses and unchanged Winbase/kernelbase/ntdll error accessors use real TEB+0x68. The old Unix slot save/restore and saved host_slot13 field are not indicated. Its explicit PE GS reads would be redundant under the whole-base model, rather than evidence that a second mirrored LastError exists.

conditionalMixingHazard.evidence: No host_qos, host_slot13 or set_teb_fiber_data identifier appears in the four reviewed canonical files. Their absence was checked directly.

layoutConflict.observation: Current char syscall_dispatch is asserted at TEB+0x340, the old fixed QWORD host_qos location. Blind field insertion or retention of old fixed-offset swaps would violate the current layout or its base-selection assumptions.

conditionalMixingHazard.scope: This identifies an ABI-porting hazard, not a current applied P1/P2 defect and not authorization to remove or change v0 patches/user engines.

remainingGaps.gap: No current built binary, generated syscall stubs, linker binding, compiler signal prologue, private TSD API execution or actual GSBASE state was inspected. The source mechanism is not a runtime pass or proof of all register preservation under Rosetta.

mac_thread_gsbase can return NULL on thread_info failure and init_syscall_frame stores it without a local failure branch; the raw TSD syscalls also have no inspected error branch. Successful native-base capture and platform syscall behavior remain source preconditions, with failure behavior unverified here. This upstream source caveat does not justify reintroducing the old slot mirrors.

Fiber and LastError coherence across syscall/Unix fast and context returns, nested callbacks, instrumentation, asynchronous signals, native host TLS/QoS use and thread start still need their own applicable runtime evidence. No existing probe or game result is borrowed from the legacy patch prose or observation JSON.

This audit maps the macOS x86_64 paths. It does not validate i386/WoW64 FS transitions, ARM64/FEX, foreign callbacks bypassing these boundaries, all assembly unwind behavior or all msync cancellation/recovery semantics.

profileProbeReview.reviewKind: bounded read-only actual-test-source and profile-args runner integration review
profileProbeReview.summary: The expected child argv cases and 23-check successful-path inventory match the source. One P2 remains: failed child termination/reap kills only the probe, without independently enforced child containment or guaranteed runner cleanup for a normal nonzero probe exit.

findings.title: Retain enforced child cleanup when termination or its follow-up wait fails
findings.trigger: The 10-second process wait does not establish exit, then TerminateProcess on that child fails or the 5-second termination wait still does not establish exit.
findings.evidence: Line 48 immediately calls fatal on either condition. fatal terminates GetCurrentProcess(), which is the probe parent, and has no child handle, job or other child containment to enforce cleanup. Parent termination is not child termination. In the inspected runner, stop-runtime cleanup is conditional on host timeout, timing discontinuity or launch error; a completed CLI response reporting the probe failure alone does not enter that cleanup block.
findings.impact: A still-running or not-yet-terminated owned child can outlive the failed probe. The owned key also bypasses its normal deletion path. The fixture can therefore violate its stated never-exit-past-a-live-owned-child guarantee; rejecting the incomplete receipt does not itself clean up that child.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide independently enforced owned-child containment before the child can execute, and require confirmed cleanup when termination/reap is unprovable. Also arrange owned-lab cleanup for failed/abnormal profile-args probe exits in the runner, rather than relying only on the host-timeout path. A parent self-termination must not be treated as child-reap confirmation.
findings.evidenceBoundary: A source failure-path defect, not an observed orphan or runtime reproduction. An unreviewed outer controller might perform later cleanup, but that does not establish this probe guarantee or the inspected runner failure path.

primaryContracts.title: Microsoft TerminateProcess
primaryContracts.supports: Terminating another process is asynchronous; waiting on its process handle establishes completion. Pending I/O can delay exit.

primaryContracts.title: Microsoft ExitProcess
primaryContracts.supports: Exiting a process does not cause its child processes to terminate.

ownershipAndNormalCleanup.observation: The key derives from the running executable basename. The probe proceeds with writes/deletion only after RegCreateKeyExW returns REG_CREATED_NEW_KEY. An already-existing key is closed and rejected before writing or deleting its value.

CreateProcessW uses the probe executable itself, with no handle inheritance. On the normal path, waiting for the process proves completion before its handles are closed. GetExitCodeProcess failure is recorded as a non-success child code after completion was established.

Registry-write failure breaks to attempted close/delete. Unexpected child argv/exit records failure and the loop continues, with each successfully reaped child completed before the next case. Close/delete are checked before the complete record. Fatal self-exit paths are the exception identified above.

profileProbeFinalReview.reviewKind: bounded actual-source read-only P2 closure review
profileProbeFinalReview.summary: The prior P2 is closed under the explicit run-mac.py --suite profile-args execution contract. The suite now drains the owned runtime on ordinary success/failure as well as interruption, and acceptance requires its confirmed cleanup receipt plus the final clock check. No remaining concrete P1/P2 found in these reviewed changes. This is not a standalone no-orphan guarantee or runtime cleanup verification.

previousFinding.resolution: The accepted design changes the execution/cleanup boundary rather than introducing a child job. The C probe explicitly requires this suite. A failed/unconfirmed child reap remains a failed probe, and the wrapper performs owned-root cleanup instead of treating parent self-termination as child completion.

closureEvidence.observation: The header now distinguishes normal per-child joining from unprovable reaping, explicitly requires the profile-args suite and no longer claims standalone no-orphan behavior.

args.suite==profile-args independently enters the stop-runtime block. That condition covers ordinary CLI success and failure as well as the existing timeout, launch-error and timing-discontinuity paths.

Cleanup confirmation requires helper exit 0, no unconfirmed client reap, receipt mode stop-runtime, literal hostShutdown.confirmed:true, empty pending, and emptyObservations>=2. Helper OS/JSON/timeout errors set confirmed:false. The complete cleanup receipt is retained in ownedRootCleanup.

passed additionally requires ownedRootCleanup.confirmed is True for profile-args. CLI exit 0, complete.ok:true, exact successful check inventory, established session binding and the other existing failure gates remain required. A baseline semantic negative cannot become passed merely because cleanup succeeded.

The final active and wall elapsed times are sampled from the original prelaunch starts after cleanup and log/metadata inspection, immediately before acceptance. Their clock-discontinuity result is ORed with the earlier result, so earlier clock failures remain sticky and the final totals include cleanup.

The 23-check inventory is retained: one new-owned-key check, ten registry-write checks, ten scenario result checks, and registry close/delete. Current C argv cases and normal cleanup logic retain the previously reviewed expectations.

profileProbeFinalReview.acceptedExecutionBoundary: Only the profile-args suite with confirmed owned runtime cleanup is covered by this closure. The C executable itself still self-terminates if child termination/reap cannot be proved; it is not independently contained when run unwrapped.

rendererProbeReview.summary: No concrete P1/P2 found in the reviewed D3D9 clear/readback source, COM reference lifetimes, pitch arithmetic, failure cleanup, 16-check inventory or renderer-smoke integration. The shared mandatory owned-cleanup gate still covers profile-args and now also covers renderer-smoke. Runtime rendering and cleanup have not been verified by this review.

probeReview.subject: Actual API path and limited observation
probeReview.observation: The source registers an owned window class and creates its window without WS_VISIBLE or a ShowWindow call. It calls Direct3DCreate9, requests D3DDEVTYPE_HAL with a 64x64 windowed X8R8G8B8 backbuffer, clears the target and obtains render target zero. It verifies dimensions and a supported 32-bit RGB/ARGB format, allocates a matching D3DPOOL_SYSTEMMEM offscreen plain surface, and calls GetRenderTargetData. This is an actual D3D9 API workload request, not runtime proof that any particular GPU/backend/module was used.

probeReview.subject: Readback API preconditions
probeReview.observation: The parameters request one backbuffer with COPY swap effect and leave multisampling at its zero-initialized NONE value. The checked source dimensions and the destination dimensions/format match, and the destination is an offscreen SYSTEMMEM surface. The source then locks the copy read-only instead of assuming the default-pool target is directly lockable. HRESULT failures stop the success path.

probeReview.subject: COM reference ownership and normal destruction order
probeReview.observation: All owned interface pointers start NULL. Each creation/acquisition is checked before dependent use. The GetRenderTarget-added surface reference is released once, as are the separately created copy, device and D3D9 object references. Cleanup releases copy and target before device, and device before the top-level object; no interface is used after Release. No assumption that Release must return zero is made.

probeReview.subject: Lock state and error cleanup
probeReview.observation: is_locked is set only after a successful LockRect. A failed row-layout check reaches cleanup with the surface still owned and attempts UnlockRect before Release. The normal UnlockRect is checked; if it fails, that failure remains recorded and cleanup makes a best-effort second unlock. Neither retry nor later releases can turn a failed check into a successful receipt. Cleanup retry success or API error-path release behavior is not asserted without runtime evidence. Window destruction and class unregistration follow COM cleanup and are checked.

probeReview.subject: Pitch arithmetic and pixel access
probeReview.observation: INT pitch is widened to int64_t before negation, avoiding INT_MIN negation overflow. The source requires non-null bits, at least 64*4 bytes of absolute row stride and a stride such that multiplying by the maximum row index 63 fits PTRDIFF_MAX. Row addresses use the returned signed pitch, not an assumed tightly packed width. memcpy loads each 4-byte pixel without an alignment assumption. The x loop accesses offsets 0..252 within the validated 256-byte pixel row. These checks establish the arithmetic being used; the actual locked storage extent still comes from the API, and no requirement that every returned pitch be negative, positive-only or exactly 256 is invented.

probeReview.subject: Integer RGB comparison
probeReview.observation: For the accepted X8R8G8B8/A8R8G8B8 layouts, the loop compares only the low 24 RGB bits against 0x2589c7 and requires all 4096 pixels to match. It deliberately does not impose a value on the X/alpha byte. The test contains no shader draw, Present, frame pacing or timing/FPS measurement.

probeReview.subject: Failure acceptance boundary
probeReview.observation: Failed setup/readback/lock/layout checks accumulate failure and enter cleanup. A color mismatch still attempts unlock and cleanup. Output failure self-terminates with nonzero status, relying on the required wrapper for runtime draining. A complete record alone is not sufficient; the runner also requires exit 0 and confirmed cleanup. COM/driver calls and output do not have an independent in-probe watchdog; the suite retains the outer timeout.

inventory.derivation: 14 main-path checks through unlock_copy plus destroy_window and unregister_class.
inventory.observation: The exact names and multiplicities match the complete success path. The runner requires 16 parsed successful checks with string names and integer actual/expected values, together with one begin/complete, the requested pointer width, correctness mode, subject d3d9-readback, complete checks 16, zero failures and no output error. Early failures produce a rejected shorter or failed receipt.

runnerIntegrationReview.observation: renderer-smoke is an allowed suite, selects renderer-smoke-<arch>.exe, copies it into the owned prefix, accepts correctness mode only and passes no guest arguments. requires_owned_cleanup is true for exactly profile-args and renderer-smoke.

Both mandatory-cleanup suites enter stop-runtime after ordinary success/failure as well as interruption. Confirmation requires helper exit 0, no unconfirmed client reap, stop-runtime receipt mode, hostShutdown.confirmed:true, no pending processes and at least two empty observations. Helper failures cannot supply a confirmed cleanup result.

The parser retains begin/check/complete and the new adapter row. Vendor/device IDs and the explicit default_choice_not_backend_detection flag are diagnostic source output; the adapter row is not treated as proof of the actual renderer or fallback.

Final active/wall elapsed checks now cover both suites, including their cleanup. passed requires ownedRootCleanup.confirmed for both, alongside CLI exit 0, successful complete/inventory checks, session binding and existing JSON/log/sampler/clock gates. Cleanup success does not erase semantic or graphics failures.

primaryContractReferences.use: Count zero with null rectangles clears the viewport using the supplied ARGB color; TARGET alone avoids requiring a depth/stencil attachment.
